title: Evidence and verification domain vocabulary
description: Identifier grammars and closed vocabularies for ADR-BCP-023 evidence, verification and discrepancy records (gate OEV-01). Adding a value is additive; removing or renaming one is breaking.

evidenceRecordId.description: Opaque Control Plane-minted EvidenceRecord identifier. It embeds no organisation, person or document detail (ADR-BCP-023 section 15).

evidenceArtifactId.description: Opaque Control Plane-minted EvidenceArtifact identifier. It embeds no organisation, person or document detail (ADR-BCP-023 section 15).

evidenceSourceId.description: Opaque Control Plane-minted EvidenceSource identifier. It embeds no organisation, person or document detail (ADR-BCP-023 section 15).

evidenceClaimId.description: Opaque Control Plane-minted EvidenceClaim identifier. It embeds no organisation, person or document detail (ADR-BCP-023 section 15).

verificationCaseId.description: Opaque Control Plane-minted VerificationCase identifier. It embeds no organisation, person or document detail (ADR-BCP-023 section 15).

verificationCheckId.description: Opaque Control Plane-minted VerificationCheck identifier. It embeds no organisation, person or document detail (ADR-BCP-023 section 15).

verificationResultId.description: Opaque Control Plane-minted VerificationResult identifier. It embeds no organisation, person or document detail (ADR-BCP-023 section 15).

evidenceDiscrepancyId.description: Opaque Control Plane-minted EvidenceDiscrepancy identifier. It embeds no organisation, person or document detail (ADR-BCP-023 section 15).

evidenceReference.description: The canonical string form of a reference to an EvidenceRecord, for fields that carry evidence references as strings (for example organisation/v1 evidenceReference). Those fields still accept legacy opaque strings; a value in this form resolves to an EvidenceRecord the Control Plane holds.

verificationProviderKey.description: A retrieval or verification mechanism, for example a commercial provider. It is never the source of a fact: the source it retrieves from is (section 25).

retentionPolicyKey.description: A versioned retention policy, for example organisation-admission/v1 (sections 145-146). Its schedule is defined by gate OEV-13.

compliancePolicyRef.description: A CompliancePolicyProfile key (section 89), defined by gate OEV-10.

jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, optionally with an ISO 3166-2 subdivision suffix.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 of content at ingestion. It proves integrity and supports duplicate detection and chain of custody; it never proves authenticity, issuer authority or truth (section 16).

reasonCode.description: A machine-readable reason, safe to show to the record's authorised readers.

subjectType.description: Section 8: what evidence may concern. Evidence is not always about the organisation record itself.

subjectReference.description: The record a piece of evidence, claim, case or discrepancy concerns: a canonical Control Plane identifier of the named type, never a name.

evidenceType.description: Section 11. INTERNAL_GOVERNANCE_RECORD cites a first-party governed source (section 181), for example the Shared legal-entity registry.

evidenceStatus.description: Section 237. Content is reviewer-accessible only in the states lifecycle.yaml lists as content_accessible (AVAILABLE, SUPERSEDED, EXPIRED); never while RECEIVED, QUARANTINED, RESTRICTED or DESTROYED, and never before scanning completes (section 238).

dataClassification.description: Section 136. Sensitive natural-person evidence normally falls in the stronger classes.

sourceClass.description: Section 20. The class alone never determines acceptance: authority is per claim type and jurisdiction (sections 21-22).

claimType.description: Section 7: the proposition a claim asserts. Source authority is granted per claim type (section 21).

assertionOrigin.description: Who put the claim forward. An APPLICANT claim starts SELF_ASSERTED and is verified only by someone else's check (sections 9, 169).

claimStatus.description: The claim's current standing, set only from its current VerificationResult once verification has run. NOT_VERIFIED means insufficient evidence, never that the claim is false (section 33).

verificationPurpose.description: Section 27. Purpose limits what evidence may be collected and reused (sections 28-29).

verificationMethod.description: Section 31. Screen scraping is not a method (section 24).

verificationOutcome.description: Section 32: the central verification result vocabulary. NOT_VERIFIED is not false (section 33); CONFLICTED means reliable sources disagree materially (section 34).

verificationDimension.description: Section 35: separate questions. Integrity never implies truth (section 36).

dimensionOutcome.description: The answer to one verification dimension.

freshnessState.description: Section 70. STALE is not false (section 71). No universal TTL exists (section 69).

verificationCaseStatus.description: Section 73. NOT_VERIFIED closes a case whose evidence was insufficient for its purpose; it records no finding that a claim is false.

discrepancyResolution.description: How a reviewer resolved a discrepancy. Nothing resolves one silently (section 76); adopting a value into canonical state still follows promotion policy (section 79).
